prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create a new production atlas of exactly THREE circular process illustrations in ONE horizontal row, three equal square cells; canvas aspect3:1. The supplied image is a STYLE reference only. Match its original astronomical chromolithograph/chalk-gouache indigo fields, ivory single thin rims, grain and simple forms. True alpha outside the three circles, opaque dark indigo inside. All subjects fully enclosed. No text, letters, labels, mathematical symbols, grid, faces or hardware. These images MUST distinguish pressure resisting collapse from matter collapsing. Arrows are sparse broad painterly ivory arrows, clearly legible at72px, their triangular arrowheads must show the specified direction. Left to right:
1. Collapsing stellar core: one small dense warm-gray sphere at centre, surrounded by three broad pale streams whose THREE ARROWHEADS point INWARD and END immediately next to the sphere. Tails are farther away toward the rim. A very faint dark orange broken shell surrounds it as stellar context. No outward rays or jets. This is inward motion compressing a core, not an explosion.
2. Pressure in dense neutron-rich matter: a compact cluster of many small packed warm-ivory particles in the middle. Exactly THREE broad arrows begin close to this dense cluster and point OUTWARD toward the upper, lower-left and lower-right circle perimeter. Arrowheads are at the OUTER ends, farthest from the centre; tails originate near the dense cluster. Absolutely NO inward arrowheads. Show matter resisting compression, not gravity compressing it. Keep ample dark indigo surrounding space.
3. Stellar pulsation: one large soft orange evolved star, same sphere shown with a faint smaller inner ghost contour and a faint larger outer ghost contour, indicating changing radius. At its upper and lower edge, two SHORT arrows point OUTWARD. At its left and right edge, two SHORT arrows point INWARD. Thus BOTH contraction and expansion directions are visible. Do not show four outward arrows or permanent winds; no jets, disk, nucleus diagram or second separate star.
